hypotheses.justification: CharP.char_is_prime_or_zero k p gives p.Prime ∨ p = 0. In the prime case, install Fact p.Prime and use the existing proof. For p = 0, choose D = C: its finite, nonempty underlying group has positive cardinality, so ¬ 0 ∣ Nat.card C. Subgroup.relIndex_self and Nat.factorization_zero_right give the index equality, since 0 ^ 0 = 1; the Grothendieck-group equality reduces to x = 1 • x. This also covers trivial C.
